findings.risk: Allows ICMP traffic from any source to any destination, which can enable network reconnaissance, host discovery, and certain denial-of-service or tunneling techniques across the environment.
findings.remediation: Restrict the stateful rule in rule_group.rules_source.rules_string from `pass icmp any any -> any any` to only the required source and destination CIDRs, and if possible specific ICMP types/codes. For example, replace `any any -> any any` with defined internal network variables or IP sets representing approved monitoring or diagnostic endpoints.

findings.issue: Broad HTTPS allow rule bypasses domain restriction
findings.risk: The rule `pass tcp any any <> $EXTERNAL_NET 443` permits generic TCP traffic on port 443 to any external destination before the TLS SNI domain restriction is evaluated, allowing outbound encrypted connections to arbitrary hosts and defeating the intended `.amazon.com` restriction.
findings.remediation: Remove or tightly scope the broad TCP 443 pass rule in `rule_group.rules_source.rules_string`. Keep only domain-restricted TLS rules, or replace `pass tcp any any <> $EXTERNAL_NET 443` with rules limited to approved destination CIDRs or fully qualified domain-based controls that align with the intended access policy.
